# Riftland Rair

Riftland Rair: an editorial fashion look (real skin, studio light, film grain) that Riftland applies on top of a Seedream model.

## Use it for

- Portraits and fashion photos of people with an editorial look
- Profile pictures and creator photos with real skin texture
- Lookbook and magazine-style shots
- A consistent house look across many photos

## Pick something else when

- Product shots or design with exact text: pick a typography or photoreal model.
- Changing an existing image without restyling it: pick a model that edits references.
- Illustration, anime or any non-photographic style: pick a model suited to it.

## Strengths

- Riftland adds a curated editorial look to every prompt: natural skin, soft studio light and film grain, with no work from you. [R]
- The same look every time, so a set of photos reads as one shoot. [R]

## Watch out for

- The look is fixed and added after your prompt, so a different lens, grade or style fights it. [R]
- It restyles whatever it is given, so it is not used to change an existing image. [R]

Evidence marks: [V] the vendor's own claim; [I] an independent report; [R] what Riftland's catalog or pipeline enforces.

## How to prompt it

- **Order:** Describe the person, the pose, the wardrobe and the setting. Riftland adds the photographic look after your text.
- **Length:** Short to medium: the subject, the clothes, the place. The look is already supplied.
- **Exact words:** Not built for exact words in the image. For a headline or a label, pick a typography model.
- **References:** References are sent along and the look is added on top, so they come out restyled: use them for the person or the place, not for an exact copy.
- **Leaving things out:** Riftland sends no separate exclusion field for this model. Say what you want in the scene and leave the rest out.

Tips:
- Spend your words on the person, the wardrobe and the setting.
- Describe the mood and the pose; the light and the grain come with the look.
- Attach a reference for the person or the place when you have one.

Avoid:
- Describing the lens, the film stock, the skin texture or the lighting: Riftland adds them, and a second description fights the first.
- Asking for a non-photographic style such as illustration or anime.

## Examples

**Ask:** An editorial portrait of a woman in a camel coat on a city street.

```text
A woman in a long camel coat walking along a quiet city street in the early evening, one hand in her pocket, looking just past the camera, a few lit shop windows behind her.
```

No lens or light: Riftland adds the editorial look.

**Ask:** A lookbook shot of a man in a linen suit by the sea.

```text
A man in a cream linen suit leaning on a white railing by the sea, loosened collar, relaxed smile, a blurred coastline behind him.
```

## Facts

- Reference images: up to 8
- Can change an existing image: no
- Aspect ratios: 1:1, 16:9, 9:16, 4:3, 3:4, 21:9
- Speed: normal
- Repeatable with a seed: yes
- Riftland adds a look of its own to the prompt: yes
- Director tags (provisional): portrait
- Recommended pick for: Portrait
- Riftland appends its editorial look to every prompt, so this model is never picked to change an existing image.

## In its family

The styled preset of the family: pick it for people in an editorial look. Pick the character model when the same person must appear across scenes, and a photoreal model for plain photos.

Same family: Rift ID · LoRA.
